findings.reason: citing the owner turns §8 into one call plus a limb mesh, and removes its criterion (2) from the work entirely.
findings.text: §8 says the limb field is evaluated "with nova's 3D Biot-Savart route" and requires the toroidal average to match the axisymmetric §6 result to 2 %, but nova already owns both: `nova/biot/toroidalaverage.py:toroidal_points` (:23), `frame_magnetic_field` (:43, a `Target` plus `Solve` over `Bx`/`By`/`Bz` through `nova/biot/space.py:Segment`), and `average_toroidal_field` (:61) returning `ToroidalAverage(radial, toroidal, vertical, residual_rms)` (:14). The plan cites none of them, so §8's route and its own acceptance comparison would both be built again beside the existing machinery.

findings.reason: naming the one module that hides the record shape, the mesh and the solve is what makes the §4 node reviewable; without it the section's depth is decided by the implementing worker rather than the design.
findings.text: §4 sets out four substantially different behaviours — read each `iron_core` segment's outline, material and B-H table; mesh without slivers; fit a monotone law with `dB/dH > 0` holding its end values; Newton-solve `F(M) = M − c(|B|)B` — in one six-hour section that names no module, so the surface will distribute into whichever of `nova/imas`, `nova/biot` or `nova/equilibrium` is nearest at the time.

findings.reason: §6 is the section most likely to leak into every read path in the package, and a named seam converts it from an instruction to touch everything into one addition.
findings.text: §6 specifies the integration as "wherever a CoilSet solves grid or point targets", which is an unbounded edit surface across every solve path rather than one entry point; §7 and §8 likewise name no file.

findings.reason: (a) alone can delete §2 and §3 — six plus five of the plan's forty-three hours — if the measurement goes the way the existing exact kernel suggests, and the other four each convert a new mechanism into an extension of one that already exists.
findings.text: five duplicate owners, listed as one census: (a) §2's thin conic sheet kernel in a new `nova/biot/sheet.py` beside `nova/biot/polygonanalytic.py`, which already implements the *exact* Urankar Part V closed form of a polygon-section ring for flux and for both field components, with corners, flux moments and the same arsinh remainders — a magnetised cell's edge is an arbitrarily thin polygon, and §2's own done-when (3) is precisely the ε→0 measurement that would settle whether Part V already delivers the sheet, yet §2 commits six hours to a parallel kernel before that measurement; (b) §2's citation of the elliptic route is to `nova/biot/polygonanalytic.py` in the plan's text while the owners are `nova/biot/completeelliptic.py:complete_kind` (:247), `nova/biot/completeelliptic.py:complete_pole` (:286) and the third-kind constant cache at `nova/biot/constants.py:Constants.np2_pole` (:438) / `Constants.Pi` (:514, `complete_pole` for characteristics 1 to 3), with the partial-range Π at `nova/biot/incompleteelliptic.py:incomplete_pole` (:266) — eq 22a's K, E and Π all exist and are cached, and the plan names none of them; (c) §4's Newton on `B = B_ext + G M` with a dense Jacobian and backtracking grades is the shape of `nova/equilibrium/reduced_newton.py` (module docstring, `external + P @ j` amplitudes, `jax.jacfwd` dense Jacobian, production backtracking grades, `ReducedNewtonStep` :299), which the plan does not cite; (d) §4's `iron_core` read has no owner, and the tree already carries two forked readers of it — `scripts/prototypes/iron_magnetisation/west.py:31` and `scripts/west_stray_field/solve.py:57` — while `nova/imas/machine.py` owns machine-description reading through `MachineGeometryReader` (:271) / `ImasGeometryReader` (:294) / `StaticMachineDescription` (:553) and knows nothing of `iron_core`, so §4 would add a third copy rather than extend the owner; (e) §8's toroidal average and 3D field route, above.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §2's new module is genuinely deep, but §4 bundles four distinct behaviours into one section with no owning module named, and §6, §7 and §8 each name no file, so the design has no home for the complexity it is adding.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — five separate mechanisms the plan would add already have an owner in the tree, led by §2's sheet kernel beside the exact Part V closed form in `nova/biot/polygonanalytic.py`; the census is below.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; against a zero baseline the plan adds a new public module, a fourth tile kind, a new source type, a material law and a mesher, and no section names what it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searches nova for the sheet kernel and the tile it will extend, but does not search for the 3D field and toroidal-average route it needs in §8, the elliptic-integral and third-kind owners §2 depends on, the Newton precedent §4 reproduces, or the machine-description reader §4 will add a third copy of.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one thin layer the plan does propose, §3's sheet tile beside the existing polygon and arc tiles in `nova/biot/tiledassembly.py`, is correctly argued as an extension of the existing tile plan, padding, device placement and compilation cache (`_fill_tile` :381, `_fill_moment_tile` :410, `_fill_arc_tile` :436) rather than a bespoke driver, which is the honest form.
